AWARD FACTUAL MATRIX & PLEADINGS 1.

The proceedings in the present case arise from the filing of the DAR by the IO in FIR No.121/2023 PS Kirti Nagar regarding the road vehicular accident which took place on 26.05.2023 at Radhe Shyam Tempo on Bhakkar Road.

As per the documents annexed with the DAR, on 26.05.2023 at Radhe Shyam Tempo on Bhakkar Road at about 1:25 pm, Eco Sport Car of red colour bearing registration no. DL1CU-318 (hereinafter referred as "offending vehicle") being ridden rashly and negligently by respondent no.1 at a very high speed hit a pedestrian Sh. Shyam Dev (hereinafter "deceased") from back, due to which the deceased sustained fatal injuries.
The deceased was taken to the hospital by one Sh. Manik Sharma and his friend Ayush who was the eye witnesses of the accident in their own vehicle where he was declared brought dead.
2. DAR mentions the respondent no.01 as driver-cum- owner and respondent no.02 as the insurer of offending vehicle.
Alongwith DAR, the final report under Section 173 Cr. PC, FIR, Site plan, PM report, seizure memos, statements of witnesses under Section 161 Cr. PC etc, were annexed.
In the final report, respondent no.1 was charge-sheeted with the offences punishable under Section 279/304A IPC.

Before adverting to the facts of the case, at the very outset, it would be apposite to note here that strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.
The standard of proof is not as strict as in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities only.
In fact, the burden of proof in a claim petition under the M.V. Act, is even lesser than a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the proposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case of "Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors." (2009) 13 SC 530, "Parmeshwari Vs.

Before adverting to the facts of the case, at the very outset, it would be apposite to note here that strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.
The standard of proof is not as strict as in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities only.
In fact, the burden of proof in a claim petition under the M.V. Act, is even lesser than a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the proposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case of "Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors." (2009) 13 SC 530, "Parmeshwari Vs.
